question: When we say a daily diet has "adequacy," what does that mainly mean?

options.A: Consuming fewer calories than you burn each day
options.B: Limiting your food intake to only one meal type
options.C: Buying expensive imported food items regularly
options.D: Eating enough essential nutrients to meet bodily needs

explanation: Spot on! Adequacy simply means your diet gives you enough energy and all the vital nutrients your body needs to stay healthy and strong. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h1)

question: Why do we encourage variety when planning daily meals?

options.A: It helps prevent eating too much of any single nutrient
options.B: It guarantees that food costs will remain very low
options.C: It ensures the body burns fat twice as fast
options.D: It removes the need to drink water with meals

explanation: Great job! Eating a nice mix of different foods keeps you from relying on just one thing, lowering the risk of missing out on some nutrients or overloading on another. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h1)

question: What is the main job of carbohydrates in our bodies?

options.C: Providing the main source of daily energy
options.D: Repairing damaged muscle tissues and bones

explanation: You got it! Carbs break down into glucose, which is your brain's and muscles' favorite and most efficient fuel for the day. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h2)

question: A patient is healing from major surgery. Which nutrient should you make sure they get more of to help their tissues repair?
explanation: Spot on! Protein acts as the building blocks needed to fix cells, fight off infection, and rebuild damaged skin and muscles. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h2)

question: Iron, calcium, and potassium belong to which group of nutrients?
explanation: Correct! These are essential minerals that help keep your bones strong, fluids balanced, and body reactions running smoothly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h3)

question: What is the main difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: If they come from plant or animal sources
options.B: How fast they dissolve in the bloodstream
options.C: The total amount the body requires daily
options.D: Whether they can provide energy to the body

explanation: You got it! Macro means large (needed in grams), while micro means small (needed in tiny milligram or microgram amounts). [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h3)

question: Which of these is usually the first noticeable sign that an adult is getting dehydrated?
explanation: Spot on! When water is low, your kidneys hold onto as much fluid as they can, turning your urine a concentrated, dark yellow or brown. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h4)

question: Why are elderly patients often at a higher risk of becoming dehydrated?

options.A: Water moves faster through older digestive tracts
options.B: Their bodies require less water than teenagers
options.C: They store more water in their skin tissues
options.D: They often experience a reduced sense of thirst

explanation: Correct! As people age, their natural thirst cue slows down, meaning they might not feel thirsty even when their body desperately needs water. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h4)

question: What is the main reason we use food guides in clinical and community nursing?

options.A: Controlling the market prices of agricultural crops
options.B: Ensuring every citizen eats the exact same calorie count
options.C: Translating nutrition science into practical meal advice
options.D: Restricting people from eating local cultural dishes

explanation: You nailed it! Food guides take confusing science and turn it into simple, colourful pictures and tips that everyday families can use. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h5)

question: In Nigeria, why do nutrition educators often suggest combining beans and grains in a meal?

options.A: To make the cooking process take significantly less time
options.B: To prevent the grains from spoiling in hot weather
options.C: To reduce the total carbohydrate content of the pot
options.D: To provide a complete complement of essential amino acids

explanation: Spot on! Plant foods alone might miss certain building blocks, but combining beans and grains fills those gaps to give you fantastic quality protein. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h5)

question: Which nutrient is especially important early in pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects?
explanation: Correct! Folic acid is a hero in early pregnancy because it helps the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h6)

question: Why do older adults generally need fewer calories each day compared to younger adults?

options.A: Their digestive systems stop absorbing carbohydrates
options.B: Their basal metabolic rate and physical activity decrease
options.C: They store all their energy directly as water weight
options.D: Their bodies no longer use fat for energy storage

explanation: You got it! As we age, we tend to lose a bit of muscle and move around less, meaning our bodies naturally burn fewer calories overall. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h6)

question: Taking a patient's height, weight, and body mass index (BMI) falls under which type of assessment?
explanation: Spot on! "Anthropometric" is just the clinical term for measuring the size, weight, and proportions of the human body. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h7)

question: If you want to know everything a hospitalized patient ate over the past 24 hours, which tool should you use?
explanation: Correct! A 24-hour dietary recall simply has the patient walk you through every single food and drink they had since yesterday. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h7)

question: What is the best nursing action for a patient who cannot safely swallow food by mouth?

options.A: Forcing the patient to finish meals to maintain weight
options.B: Waiting until the patient asks for intravenous fluids
options.C: Stopping all fluid and medication administration
options.D: Managing alternative feeding methods like enteral tubes

explanation: You got it! When swallowing is unsafe, nurses step in to manage alternative routes—like a nasogastric (NG) tube—to keep the patient nourished safely. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h8)

question: Why is keeping a hospital ward calm and clean during mealtime so important?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to clean bedsheets
options.B: It speeds up the digestion rate in the stomach
options.C: It stops patients from talking to one another
options.D: It encourages better appetite and food consumption

explanation: Spot on! A peaceful, clean, and pleasant dining vibe lowers stress and makes patients actually want to eat their meals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h8)
